# @codenhub/jwt

> JwtKit: JSON Web Token (compact JWS) signing and verification on Web Crypto, for tokens that must be treated as untrusted, with key generation, import and export, key sets, remote JWKS and key rotation. Signs and verifies ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA, Ed25519, RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, HS256, HS384 and HS512; `none` is never accepted. No runtime dependencies; runs on Node.js 26 or newer, browsers and edge runtimes. The package is experimental.

Every key is bound to exactly one algorithm when it is generated (`generateKeyPair`, `generateSecretKey`) or imported (`importPublicKey`, `importPrivateKey`, `importKeyPair`, `importSecretKey`, from a JWK, a PEM in SPKI, PKCS#8, PKCS#1, SEC 1 or a certificate, or a Web Crypto `CryptoKey`); a token verifies only with a key whose `alg` equals its header's `alg`. Keys are opaque frozen objects (`kind` is `public`, `private` or `secret`); only objects this package created are accepted, and only by the same copy of the package, so a program must load one copy (dedupe the install; a library built on it declares it as a `peerDependency`). `kid: "thumbprint"` names a key by its RFC 7638 thumbprint; `jwkThumbprint` computes it, and `exportPublicJwk`, `exportPrivateJwk` and `exportSecretJwk` export keys as JWKs.

`createVerifier({ keys, issuer, subject, audience, type, requireExpiration, allowExpired, clockTolerance, maxAge, maxLength, requiredClaims, claims, now, onKeySetError })` returns `verify(token)`, which resolves to `{ ok: true, value: { header, payload, key } }` or `{ ok: false, error: { issues } }` and never throws for a token; only a `claims` schema that throws or rejects makes it reject. A token without `exp`, or with an `aud` when no `audience` is set, fails unless waived. Durations are seconds; `now` returns milliseconds. Checks run in order: length cap (default 8192), strict base64url and JSON (duplicate keys rejected, depth 32), supported `alg`, no `crit`, key selection, signature, then claims (all claim failures reported together), then the optional Standard Schema `claims`. There is no unverified payload decode; `readHeader(token)` returns only the header. `sign({ payload, key, header, issuedAt, notBefore, expiresIn, jti, now })` takes `alg` from the key and adds only the claims its options ask for. `embedKey` writes the signing key's public JWK into the header, as a DPoP proof (RFC 9449) carries it.

Key sets: `createKeySet(keys)`, `importKeySet(jwks, { algorithms, issuer })`, `createRemoteKeySet({ url, fetch, algorithms, issuer, cacheTtl, cooldown, maxStale, timeout, maxResponseBytes, now, seed, onFetch, onFetchError, waitUntil })` for an https JWKS URL with caching that honours `max-age`, a refetch on unknown `kid` limited by a cooldown, and stale keys while the issuer is unreachable, and a `keys` function from the claimed `iss` to a key set or route. Selection never tries keys in turn. `createKeyRing` schedules an issuer's signing keys and publishes its JWKS.

JWE, the JWS JSON serialization, unencoded payloads and `crit` extensions are rejected. Issues have a stable `code`, optional `path` and `params`, and the package's own issues never contain input values; a `claims` schema's path may name payload properties, and a custom key set's issues are passed through. Invalid options and foreign key objects throw `TypeError`.

## Documentation

- [Documentation overview](docs/index.md): What a JWT is, algorithm binding, the result shape, the check order, and requirements.
- [Verifying tokens](docs/verifying.md): Every `createVerifier` option, check order, time claims and clock tolerance, issuer, subject, audience and `typ` matching, Standard Schema claims, and `readHeader`.
- [Signing tokens](docs/signing.md): What `sign` writes into the header, refused header parameters, the payload rules, the claims it adds when asked, and token hashes.
- [Keys](docs/keys.md): Key kinds, generating, importing JWKs, PEM, Web Crypto keys and raw secrets with the checks and issues of each, exporting, and thumbprints.
- [Key sets](docs/key-sets.md): Selection rules, local sets, importing a JWKS, choosing a key set by issuer, and remote JWKS caching, cooldown, stale keys and fetch failures.
- [Key rotation](docs/rotation.md): Rotating an issuer's signing keys with `createKeyRing`, publishing each key before and after it signs, and replacing a leaked key.
- [Issues](docs/errors.md): The result shape and every issue code with its path and params, and what throws instead.
